purpose: Author/AI-assisted exploratory evidence labels for exercising the fact-check workflow. This is not independent gold and must not be used to report system accuracy.

limitations: The project author selected and interpreted the evidence with AI assistance.
Several reports repeat agency statements and are not fully independent primary investigations.
Dynamic social-media counts and unauthenticated screenshots are treated conservatively.
Independent adjudicators must still review the frozen claims before system accuracy is reported.

pilot.rationale: Two publishers quote ADOR announcing preparations to resume music activities on April 27.
Both reports attribute the Copenhagen pre-production description directly to ADOR.
Separate reports record ADOR's May 7 statement that internal discussions were continuing.
A news agency and public broadcaster agree on the amount and three named defendant groups.
The legal filing and an independent legal summary establish that these similarities were alleged; they do not prove plagiarism.
Two timestamped reports document the four-member anniversary video and photos on July 22.
A news agency and public broadcaster report ADOR's termination announcement.
Vietnamese and Korean reports independently recorded matching one-day Instagram counts, but the underlying metrics are dynamic.
The December termination announcement and subsequent damages filing are documented by separate outlets.
Two publishers report the named designer's public criticism; this verifies the attribution, not the subjective judgment.
Both sources support the roughly 43 billion won filing. The dollar conversion varies with exchange rate, so $31 million is approximate.
Minji appeared in anniversary content, but two July 22 reports explicitly say her return was not confirmed.
The press-conference report and members' statement agree on the November 2024 notification and alleged breaches.
Haerin and Hyein were confirmed in November and Danielle was terminated in December, but Hanni's confirmation came in December, not November.
Two April 27 reports quote ADOR describing the Copenhagen visit as pre-production for a new musical journey.
Two court reports agree on the 43.1 billion won action and Thursday hearing; the dollar figure is a dated conversion.
Two previews said the defendants were not expected in person, and the later hearing report confirms only representatives attended.
Two outlets document that Shakatak made the allegation in 2024; the label disputed it.
The contemporaneous report and official member statement agree on the November 2024 termination notice.
Separate reports quote ADOR calling the video commemorative and postponing detailed plans until talks conclude.
The amount and parties are supported, but reports place the filing on December 30, not early February as the relative-date phrase implies.
The ruling and contract duration through 2029 are independently reported; Newsis supplies the exact July 31 date.
A circulating reservation image is not authenticated, reported date ranges conflict, and ADOR did not confirm studio use.
pilot.search_notes: Searched Korean and English reports, the claimed studio-reservation wording, ADOR statements, and follow-up coverage. No authenticated booking record or primary confirmation was found.

pilot.rationale: Two publishers quote ADOR directly confirming the members' Copenhagen visit with staff.
The termination date and 43.1 billion won suit are supported, but publishers conflict on whether the suit was filed December 29 or 30.
Two reports confirm all members let the appeal deadline pass after losing the October first-instance case.
Two publications identify All Surface Publishing and accurately frame copying as the plaintiff's allegation.
Both sources identify Samir's Theme as DJ Debonair Samir's 2005 track.
Two Korean publishers document ADOR's anniversary film release on July 22.
Two reports attribute the fan-celebration purpose to ADOR; one preserves the members' shared-wish wording.
